content:
The [Income Tax Calculator](/income-tax-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Estimate your US federal income tax for 2025, with effective and marginal rates. Enter your filing status, annual income (gross) and deductions and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

A federal income tax calculator estimates what you owe the IRS for 2025: it subtracts your deductions from your gross income, then applies the federal tax brackets to the remainder. The 2025 standard deductions are $15,750 for single filers, $31,500 for married couples filing jointly and $23,625 for heads of household. The result shows your total tax, your effective rate (tax as a share of all your income) and your marginal bracket — the rate on your next dollar. This is an estimate based on the 2025 US federal brackets and standard deduction. It is not tax advice — your real tax depends on credits, state rules and your full situation, so check important figures with a tax professional.

## How to use the Income Tax Calculator

Start by choosing your filing status from the list, then entering your annual income (gross) and finally entering your deductions. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Choose your filing status: single, married filing jointly, or head of household.
2. Enter your total annual gross income — wages, plus any other income you expect.
3. Enter your deductions. The field starts at the 2025 standard deduction for a single filer; enter your itemised total instead if it is higher.
4. Check the estimated tax, the effective rate and your marginal bracket.

## Formula

Taxable income = gross income − deductions. Tax is calculated bracket by bracket: 10% up to $11,925, 12% to $48,475, 22% to $103,350, 24% to $197,300, 32% to $250,525, 35% to $626,350 and 37% above that (single filer, 2025). Effective rate = tax ÷ gross income.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Income Tax Calculator](/income-tax-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A single filer earning $85,000 with the $15,750 standard deduction has $69,250 of taxable income. The tax is $1,192.50 at 10%, plus $4,386 at 12%, plus $4,570.50 at 22% — $10,149 in total, an effective rate of 11.94% and a marginal bracket of 22%. After-tax income is $74,851. Try the same figures in the [Income Tax Calculator](/income-tax-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Filing status: Single, Annual income (gross): 85000, Deductions: 15750), the [Income Tax Calculator](/income-tax-calculator) returns Estimated federal tax: 10,149, Effective tax rate: 11.94%, Marginal tax bracket: 22%, Taxable income: 69,250, After-tax income: 74,851. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## How the 2025 brackets work

The US taxes income in slices. Only the income inside each bracket is taxed at that bracket's rate — so moving into the 22% bracket does not mean all your income is taxed at 22%. For a single filer in 2025, the first $11,925 is taxed at 10%, the slice from $11,925 to $48,475 at 12%, and so on up to 37% above $626,350. Your marginal bracket is the rate on your last dollar; your effective rate is the average across all slices, and it is always lower than your marginal rate.

## Standard deduction vs itemising

The standard deduction is a fixed amount the IRS lets you subtract from your income before tax — $15,750 for single filers in 2025. Itemising means adding up deductible expenses (mortgage interest, state taxes up to a cap, charitable gifts and more) and using that total instead, but only if it is higher than the standard deduction. Most filers take the standard deduction because it is simpler and, for most people, larger.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Your marginal bracket is what matters for decisions like Roth vs traditional retirement contributions — not your effective rate.
- Contributions to a traditional 401(k) or IRA lower your taxable income, so they lower your tax bill this year.
- Tax credits (child tax credit, education credits) reduce your tax directly, dollar for dollar — they are worth more than deductions of the same size.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is this tax advice?

No. This is an estimate from the published 2025 brackets and standard deduction. Real tax depends on credits, state taxes, capital gains, self-employment income and more. For anything that affects real money, check with a tax professional. Try it with your own numbers in the [Income Tax Calculator](/income-tax-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What is the difference between marginal and effective tax rate?

Your marginal rate is the tax on your next dollar of income — the top bracket you reach. Your effective rate is your total tax divided by your total income. Because lower slices are taxed at lower rates, your effective rate is always lower than your marginal rate. Try it with your own numbers in the [Income Tax Calculator](/income-tax-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Does this include state tax?

No — this is federal income tax only. State income tax is separate and varies widely; use the Paycheck Calculator if you want an estimate that includes a state figure. Try it with your own numbers in the [Income Tax Calculator](/income-tax-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Income Tax Calculator use?

Taxable income = gross income − deductions. Tax is calculated bracket by bracket: 10% up to $11,925, 12% to $48,475, 22% to $103,350, 24% to $197,300, 32% to $250,525, 35% to $626,350 and 37% above that (single filer, 2025). Effective rate = tax ÷ gross income. You can see it in action in the [Income Tax Calculator](/income-tax-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Income Tax Calculator?

Just Filing status, Annual income (gross) and Deductions. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
